text:
dana: quick question — we need to lock down who can see tenant audit events before the schema change lands. Proposed rules: tenant admins see only their tenant; org admins see everything; support can get scoped, time-limited access (with approval). also: customer-facing audit exports need to be signed/validated by KMS. any objections? :thinking:

samir: sounds reasonable. couple of specifics: 
- scoped tokens MUST include tenant_id claim and audit:read scope 
- audit-reader role (for product/support) should be "read-only, no pii" by default; if they request full-events we require an approval ticket + short TTL token.

lia: nit on schema — we should add an explicit `visibility` enum and `tenant_id` to every audit event so the validation pipeline can reject cross-tenant events early. example: 
```json
{"event_ts":"2026-03-19T18:12:03Z","actor":"service-x","action":"model.deploy","tenant_id":"t-1234","visibility":"tenant"}
```
this lets downstream tooling filter without guessing from nested payloads.

mike: +1. about scoped tokens: they must be audience-limited to `audit-api` and include an `exp` <= 1h for support requests. example JWT claims: 
```
{
  "sub":"user:mike","tenant_id":"t-1234","scope":"audit:read","aud":"audit-api","exp":1710004800
}
```
we should also validate the token issuer (our auth service) in the audit service.

security-bot: automated-check: audit-validation pipeline failed for commit 7a9c2b — missing tenant_id enforcement in parser. See CI log: https://ci/internal/1234 :rotating_light:

dana: good catch @security-bot. I'll block the schema merger until parser includes tenant_id null-checks + visibility whitelist. also open question: how do we present customer-facing audit exports? signed bundle + manifest?

samir: recommend envelope signing using KMS asymmetric keys per-customer. flow: export -> manifest (list of event IDs + visibility) -> sign(manifest) with customer's public key or our KMS-wrapped key. That allows customers to verify integrity without exposing internal metadata. We'll need a small change: include `event_id` on every event for manifest references.

lia: also consider redaction policies in the export pipeline: mark PII fields with `redaction_reason` and include redaction version. customers need consistent reproducibility for compliance.

mike: edge case: org admins/enterprise SOCs request cross-tenant search. That should be allowed only via an "enterprise-audit" role and require an audit trail (who queried, why). maybe require SSO group membership + 2FA.

dana: agreed. for incident response we also need emergency access tokens (break-glass) with multi-approver workflow and automatic audit event emission when used. logging of the usage must be immutable and KMS-signed.

audit-bot: note: created ticket SEC-987 for "tenant_id enforcement" and SEC-988 for "KMS export signing design doc".

samir: action items: 
- samir: update token validator to enforce tenant_id claim + aud check (PR by EOD)
- lia: add visibility + event_id + redaction_reason to schema PR (tomorrow)
- dana: block merge and draft support access policy + break-glass flow (this week)

mike: 👍 will prototype ephemeral incident token flow with 2-approver lattice.

dana: thanks all — tagging @security-bot for follow-up CI gate once PRs are in. :lock:
